approved_exception_carrier.what: Lower the exact haxe.Exception carrier conversion members directly at typed call sites.
approved_exception_carrier.why: Caught and thrown Haxe values cross the backend exception representation, so ordinary source cannot safely recover or expose the carrier without knowing that representation.
approved_exception_carrier.how: Keep only the two exact conversion calls and route them to the typed hxrt exception carrier API.
approved_exception_carrier.reviewCondition: Revisit if staged exception source gains a typed carrier abstraction that preserves arbitrary Haxe thrown values.

approved_lambda_iterable_representation.what: Adapt exact calls to all 19 source-owned Lambda algorithms across Go's erased structural Iterable, constrained nested-Iterable, and invariant function representations.
approved_lambda_iterable_representation.why: The generated Lambda source accepts the erased map-shaped Iterable protocol, while valid Haxe callers can supply native Go slices, staged lists, concrete iterator classes, typed callbacks, and nested iterable carriers that are not assignable to the same Go shape. A constrained nested iterable additionally becomes a Go method interface that a structural map cannot implement directly.
approved_lambda_iterable_representation.how: Wrap only iterator construction, callback parameters, nested iterable values, and erased results at the call site. Use the representation-only private LambdaGoIterableCarrier companion where Go requires a nominal iterator method, and reject already-erased nested carriers with a deterministic Haxe diagnostic. Every traversal, comparison, early exit, allocation, and public algorithm remains in std/go/_std/Lambda.hx.
approved_lambda_iterable_representation.reviewCondition: Remove when generated Go models Haxe Iterable and generic function variance with one assignable typed representation.

approved_native_api.what: Keep compiler emitters used exclusively by explicit typed go.* native APIs outside the portable stdlib ownership registry.
approved_native_api.why: Native channels, collections, and Go result tuples deliberately expose Go representation and typed specialization decisions rather than portable Haxe stdlib behavior.
approved_native_api.how: List every excluded group and debt context explicitly so a new native emitter cannot be mistaken for a portable stdlib exception.
approved_native_api.reviewCondition: Revisit when typed Go IR can express the same native specialization without generated helper declarations.

approved_resource_table.what: Materialize the exact haxe.Resource.content data table from compile-time embedded resources.
approved_resource_table.why: Ordinary Haxe source can implement the Resource API, but it cannot read the compiler resource table after typing or invent the generated payload bytes.
approved_resource_table.how: Keep only data population in the compiler and let source-owned haxe.Resource methods consume the resulting field.
approved_resource_table.reviewCondition: Revisit if resource data is emitted as a typed generated artifact that staged source can import directly.

approved_rest_representation.what: Lower the two haxe.Rest slice-copy operations directly for the concrete typed element representation.
approved_rest_representation.why: The abstract operation must preserve the call-site element type while constructing a native Go slice, which is a typed representation fact unavailable to erased ordinary source.
approved_rest_representation.how: Keep only append and prepend as exact call-site representation primitives and preserve copy-on-write behavior.
approved_rest_representation.reviewCondition: Revisit when generic typed slice construction is available as an ordinary staged-source primitive.

approved_rtti_fields.what: Materialize generated __meta__ and __rtti fields from the compiler-known metadata attached to each reachable type.
approved_rtti_fields.why: The final field contents depend on typed compiler metadata and reachable generated types, which ordinary Haxe source cannot enumerate.
approved_rtti_fields.how: Generate only the metadata data access protocol; keep public RTTI parsing and traversal in staged source.
approved_rtti_fields.reviewCondition: Revisit if the metadata is emitted as typed data consumed by staged RTTI source without compiler-owned access behavior.

approved_serialization_source_bridge.what: Invoke the exact generated hxSerialize, hxUnserialize, resolveClass, and resolveEnum methods from staged serialization source inside the generated program package.
approved_serialization_source_bridge.why: Public Haxe methods intentionally compile to package-private Go methods, so an external hxrt package cannot call custom serialization hooks or structural resolver methods. Ordinary class instances also cannot be modeled as one anonymous-map shape without rejecting valid Haxe programs.
approved_serialization_source_bridge.how: Emit only exact interface assertions and anonymous resolver callback extraction when Serializer or Unserializer is reachable. Token parsing, regex behavior, traversal, caches, metadata tables, class and enum construction, reflection, unsafe access, and resolver policy remain outside this bridge.
approved_serialization_source_bridge.reviewCondition: Remove when generated public Haxe methods and structural objects share a source-visible typed invocation representation that does not require same-package adaptation.

approved_sort_erasure_representation.what: Adapt exact ArraySort and ListSort calls to their source-owned generic Haxe entrypoints.
approved_sort_erasure_representation.why: The source algorithms erase generic arrays, linked nodes, and comparators to Go any-based signatures, which are not assignable from concrete typed slices, nodes, or callbacks even though the Haxe calls are valid.
approved_sort_erasure_representation.how: Box and copy back ArraySort slices, adapt comparator parameters, and assert ListSort heads to the typed node; the stable merge-sort algorithms remain entirely in upstream Haxe source.
approved_sort_erasure_representation.reviewCondition: Remove when generic source methods retain concrete Go type parameters or the backend provides an equivalent typed generic representation.

approved_string_representation.what: Lower exact string construction and dynamic string-conversion primitives through typed hxrt helpers.
approved_string_representation.why: Go strings and Haxe nullable strings use a backend-owned representation, so these primitives must construct or inspect that representation consistently.
approved_string_representation.how: Admit only Std.string and String.fromCharCode; library parsing and formatting remain migration work.
approved_string_representation.reviewCondition: Revisit when the string representation is modeled as a typed source-facing abstraction rather than compiler knowledge.

approved_type_metadata.what: Generate narrow Type and reflection lookup declarations from the compiler's closed typed class and enum metadata tables.
approved_type_metadata.why: Ordinary Haxe source cannot enumerate the final reachable generated Go types, constructors, class markers, and enum markers at compile time.
approved_type_metadata.how: Keep metadata generation separate from public reflection algorithms and register its exact compiler entry point.
approved_type_metadata.reviewCondition: Revisit if the compiler emits a typed metadata data file that staged source can consume without generated behavior.

approved_type_test.what: Lower Std.isOfType against the compiler-known target type and generated representation.
approved_type_test.why: The second argument is a typed class, enum, or abstract token whose correct Go check depends on compile-time type and representation information.
approved_type_test.how: Require a type literal, evaluate the value once, and emit the narrow representation-aware check.
approved_type_test.reviewCondition: Revisit when all portable type tokens share a source-visible runtime descriptor with equivalent semantics.

approved_unsupported_diagnostic.what: Reject the exact Sys.cpuTime surface at Haxe compile time with an honest target-specific diagnostic.
approved_unsupported_diagnostic.why: Go's supported standard library does not expose portable process CPU time, and substituting wall time would silently violate the Haxe contract.
approved_unsupported_diagnostic.how: Detect only the typed Sys.cpuTime field and report the documented unsupported capability before Go generation.
approved_unsupported_diagnostic.reviewCondition: Remove the diagnostic if a supported, portable, dependency-safe process CPU-time capability becomes available.

migration_dispatch.what: Retire the shared portable stdlib shim dispatcher as each behavior-heavy group moves to staged source or hxrt.
migration_dispatch.why: A dispatcher is structural plumbing, not an intrinsic, and its continued existence must not make every child shim appear required.
migration_dispatch.how: Keep its debt avoidable and shrink its exact group set as the linked migrations remove entries.
migration_dispatch.reviewCondition: Remove the dispatcher when no portable declaration group remains.

migration_http.what: Move sys.Http public request and callback behavior to staged Haxe over typed native HTTP capabilities.
migration_http.why: Request sequencing, headers, payloads, proxy policy, callbacks, and response normalization are runtime and library semantics rather than compile-time facts.
migration_http.how: Keep Haxe-visible choreography in source and expose transport resources through narrow hxrt handles.
migration_http.reviewCondition: Close only when haxe_go-vfp.8.7.12 removes the generated sys.Http authority and shim group.

migration_io.what: Move the base haxe.io hierarchy, byte policy, stream methods, encoding, EOF, and error behavior out of compiler-emitted declarations.
migration_io.why: Native byte storage can require a representation boundary, but that does not require compiler ownership of complete public types and algorithms.
migration_io.how: Put public semantics in staged Haxe, cross only typed raw-byte capabilities, and individually register any smaller irreducible representation primitive.
migration_io.reviewCondition: Close only when haxe_go-vfp.8.7.11 retires the broad io group and adjudicates every residual primitive.

migration_runtime_reflection.what: Move runtime-only Reflect.fields behavior out of compiler-generated declarations.
migration_runtime_reflection.why: Field enumeration inspects runtime values and does not consume the compiler's closed metadata table.
migration_runtime_reflection.how: Use a staged helper island or narrow hxrt reflection capability while keeping generated metadata work separately registered.
migration_runtime_reflection.reviewCondition: Remove under haxe_go-vfp.8.7.15 once equivalent typed runtime behavior lands.

migration_stdlib_symbols.what: Split the remaining Unicode, Reflect, Option, logging, and nominal-symbol block by its correct source or runtime owner; crypto, XML, zip, Date, and Math have already left the group.
migration_stdlib_symbols.why: Most functions in the group are ordinary library or runtime behavior; sharing a file with generated type metadata does not make them compile-context intrinsics.
migration_stdlib_symbols.how: Move library code to upstream or staged Haxe, native algorithms to narrow hxrt helpers, and keep only separately registered metadata or representation primitives.
migration_stdlib_symbols.reviewCondition: Close only when haxe_go-vfp.8.7.15 retires lowerStdlibSymbolShimDecls and registers any exact residual primitive.
